The validation loop

Define once, test everywhere, feed the fixes back.

Comparing models by hand means re-running the same questions again and again and eyeballing every answer. The validation loop replaces that: set up a test once, run it across every model you support, compare the results in a single view, then send validated fixes — a tracked issue with a drafted change — straight back to the MCP server and skill that need them.

Models tested: Anthropic · Anthropic CLI · OpenAI · Google · Ollama · Qlik Answers

Grade every run

Every run is graded, automatically.

The moment a run finishes it is rated, with no reference answer required. That grade is what turns a pile of sessions into something you can rank, trust, and compare.

Answer validation, with evidence

Did the answer address the task? You get a verdict and a 0 to 1 score, backed by quotes lifted straight from the transcript. No black-box numbers.

Insight surplus and error forensics

Useful extra content lifts the score. Padding lowers it. A deterministic inventory catches every error, failed call, and guardrail stop.

Expectation grades when you want them

Add expectations and every run is also scored on Answer, Judge, ROUGE-1, Hygiene, and Surplus.

Measured, not guessed

Exactly what gets scored on every run.

Every run carries the same KPIs and the same grades, so any two runs sit on identical axes. That is what makes the comparisons trustworthy instead of anecdotal.

How each run is graded

An automatic base rating, plus expectation grades when a test defines them.

  • Answer validationVerdict + 0 to 1 score, cited evidence
  • Insight surplusValue added vs. padding
  • Error forensicsRoot-cause inventory + drafted fix
  • ROUGE-1Overlap with a reference answer
  • JudgeLogprob-weighted LLM judge
  • HygieneClean, well-formed tool use
  • Trajectory and SkillFlowPath and skill conformance
  • Suite consistencyVariance across repeated runs

The loop closes

Fixes flow back to the skill that caused them.

When a run grades poorly and a skill was involved, AI Workbench files a tracked issue on that skill, with a drafted fix and a link to the failing run. Resolve it, or hand it to the assistant for a new, re-testable version. Run it as a long-running quality gate and regressions get caught before a user sees them.

Answers

The questions we get on day one.

Does AI Workbench replace my model provider?

No. It drives your provider's models, or a Qlik Answers assistant, through a real agent loop and measures the result. You bring your own provider key or your Claude subscription for test runs.

What does it cost to run?

The app itself runs locally with no accounts and no cloud. The only spend is your own provider's usage when you execute test runs, and AI Workbench estimates that cost per run so there are no surprises.

How is a run graded?

Automatically, the moment it finishes: answer validation with cited evidence, insight surplus, and an error-forensics inventory. Add expectation grades (Answer, Judge, ROUGE-1, Hygiene, Surplus) when a test defines what good looks like. Every run carries the same grades, which is what makes runs comparable.

Can it really compare Qlik Answers to an MCP agent?

Yes. A Qlik Answers assistant is a first-class run target alongside any model. Run both against the same test and compare turns, tokens, cost, and quality side by side, with a plain-language verdict on the trade-off.

Where does my data go?

Nowhere it does not already go. Servers, credentials, and results stay on your machine. Saved secrets are encrypted at rest and never returned in responses. Test runs call only the providers you configure.

Do I need a Qlik tenant?

Not to analyze MCP servers, run sessions, grade, or compare. A Qlik tenant is only needed if you want to point AI Workbench at a Qlik Cloud MCP server or a Qlik Answers assistant.
